- When sentiment is high (≥0.35) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values by >5% in early days of the 30d horizon, apply a 3–5 day lag correction by subtracting 1–2% per day from the forecast.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.15) and forecast is high, apply a downward bias correction of 2–5% to align with mean reversion.  
- If forecast shows a sharp upward move followed by a steep drop, reduce the subsequent drop by 1–3% to avoid premature correction.  
- For 30d forecasts, if the first 5–7 days show high forecast values with low sentiment, reduce those early values by 3–7% to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
